comments.text:
Here is a misconception. 
China unified in 221 BC, true, but not the china of today. 
If we go by language groups, than china Unified the sino-tibetan languages only in the last century.
The european branch of the Indo-European languages, can be roughly split into the Corded ware, or flatland, or northern branch (germano-baltic), and the Urnfield, or mountainous or southern branch (Celtic, italic and most likely paleo balkanic).
The Urnfield branch was actually unified under the romans at around the same time as the Chinese first unified. Just that it never reunified after the fall of the roman empire in the west in the 5th century, whereas the sino branch of the sino tibetan languages reunified and expanded again and again after every collapse. 
Now the EU is basically a european second unification attempt including the corded ware (flatland) branch
